senses.gloss: f.(b. h.; cmp. עתד) [something fastened, driven in,] peg, nail; handle of a tool &c.
units: <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Taanit 4:1:16">Y. Taan. IV, 67ᵈ</cite> <he>אשרי אדם … י׳ להיתלות בה</he> (cmp.

<cite ref="Isaiah 22:23">Is. XXII, 23</cite>, sq.) happy the man who has a peg to hang on, i.e. who has a renowned ancestry; <he>ומה היתה יְתֵידָתוֹ וכ׳</he> and what was R. E.’s. peg?; <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 4:1:33">Y. Ber. IV, 7ᵈ</cite> top.
<cite ref="Gittin 17a:8">Gitt. 17ᵃ</cite> <he>י׳ היא שלא תמוט</he> (my last opinion) is an immovable peg.

<cite ref="Megillah 6a:12">Meg. 6ᵃ</cite> <he>והיא היתה י׳ תקועה וכ׳</he> and she (Cæsarea) was a peg driven into Israel, i.e. an obnoxious foreign element.—<he>י׳ של מחרישה</he> the pin of the plough.
Sabb. XVII, 4; a. e, v. מַחֲרֵישָׁה.—י׳ האהל tent-pin, v. infra.—י׳ הדרכים a way-mark of hardened clay pegs, v. גֵּץ; v. infra.—Pl. יְתֵדוֹת, יְתֵידוֹת.
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 43:8">Gen. R. s. 43</cite> <he>שלשה י׳ גדולות</he> three great pegs (Abraham, Isaac and Jacob).
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 62:3">Gen. R. s. 62</cite> <he>נתגרו בהן י׳ הארץ</he> the pegs of the land (the remnants of the seven nations, cmp.
<cite ref="Mishnah Kelim 14:3">Kel. XIV, 3</cite> <he>י׳ אהלים י׳ המשוחות</he> Mish. ed. (Bab. ed. <he>ידות</he>) the (metal) pegs of tents and those of the land measurers.
<cite ref="Tosefta Keilim Batra 1:7">Tosef. Kel. B. Bath. I, 7</cite> <he>החרב שפרשה עם י׳ המחרישה</he> the knife (coulter) which has been taken out with the handle of the plough.
<cite ref="Mishnah Mikvaot 9:2">Mikv. IX, 2</cite> <he>י׳ הדרכים</he>, expl. <he>גץ יוני</he>.
<cite ref="Tosefta Mikvaot 6:14">Tosef. ib. VI</cite> (<cite ref="Tosefta Mikvaot 7:14">VII</cite>), 14.

<cite ref="Bava Kamma 81a:2">B. Kam. 81ᵃ</cite> <he>מסתלקין מפני י׳ הד׳ …</he> you may (in walking) turn out from the highway towards the private sidewalk in order to avoid the road-pegs; Y. Ber. II, end, 5ᵈ top.
